threads.body:
`%ignorecase` means `yytext()` may preserve the caller’s original casing. In `DdlOperation.handleOperationTarget`, storing the raw `target` can lead to inconsistent `operationName` values (e.g., "CREATE table") and can break later equality checks against uppercase constants (e.g., the `TABLE` check that gates `recordCollectionName()`), causing `db.collection.name` to be missing for statements like `create table ...`.

Normalizing the operation target once (e.g., to uppercase) keeps operation/collection extraction stable and makes the subsequent comparisons reliable.

threads.body: `DdlOperation.hasSafeDdlTarget()` compares `operationTarget` using case-sensitive `equals(...)`, but `operationTarget` intentionally preserves the original query casing (because of `%ignorecase` + `yytext()`/`target`). For statements like `create table ...`, this makes `hasSafeDdlTarget()` return false, so PASSWORD/IDENTIFIED BY handling is applied as if the target were unsafe, leading to incorrect sanitization behavior for safe DDL targets.

replies.body: Fixed in edecfeaed7. `hasSafeDdlTarget()` now uses case-insensitive target matching in both SQL sanitizers, and there is a lowercase `create table users (password VARCHAR(255))` regression test covering this. While touching the summary sanitizer, the real operation keyword paths now record the matched token text via `yytext()` as well.

threads.body: `operationTarget` is captured from `yytext()` under `%ignorecase`, so it preserves the query’s original casing (e.g., `table`). But `hasSafeDdlTarget()` does case-sensitive comparisons against uppercase literals ("TABLE", ...), so for statements like `create table users (password ...)` it will treat PASSWORD as a secret clause and truncate/sanitize the remainder incorrectly. Make `hasSafeDdlTarget()` case-insensitive (or normalize `operationTarget` for comparisons).

threads.body: `TRUNCATE` currently never records the table identifier into `collectionName`. With `setSingleOperationAndCollection(true)`, this means `db.collection.name` will be missing for `TRUNCATE TABLE <table>` even though the statement has a single clear target.

threads.body: In the stable-semconv branch, `DB_QUERY_TEXT` and `DB_QUERY_SUMMARY` assertions expect a lowercase `select ...`, which matches the actual query casing. But `DB_OPERATION_NAME` is asserted as uppercase `"SELECT"`, which is inconsistent with the sanitizer behavior (it preserves original casing via `yytext()` under `%ignorecase`) and with the query summary assertion just below. This will make the test fail when `db.operation.name` is emitted as `"select"`.
